assignments.evidence: A compound of mk 'god' + kdi 'woman', with the doubled k merged.
kdi 'woman' + the kinship suffix -te: the female counterpart of wide 'brother'.
Recalled as the epitaph term for a spouse (wife); a short kinship noun.
A loan of Egyptian p3 mr-ms' 'overseer of the army', the Meroitic title of a general.
Recalled as the coordinating particle used in enumerations.
Recalled as the title 'scribe'; it resembles Egyptian ss 'scribe'.
A weakly recalled animal noun (bull or ox), beside dime 'cow'.
The standard Meroitic royal title (qore = sovereign, beside kdke = queen).
Recalled as 'adoration'; probably built on Egyptian dw3 'to adore'.
The kinship term wi(-de) of epitaph relationship lines (wide-lowi); same -de/-te suffix as kdite.
A weakly recalled offering-context noun ('sacrifice'); partly by elimination.
The epitaph filiation pair: mother's name + tdxe-lowi, father's name + yerike-lowi.
A kinship term with the same -de suffix, used for a collateral relative in epitaphs.
A loan of Egyptian wpwty 'messenger'; the known title of envoys (for example to Rome).
A weakly recalled direction word ('south'); partly by elimination.
The benediction 'at mXe ...' runs parallel to 'ato mXe ...' (abundant water, abundant bread).
The recalled Meroitic word for child or young person; ar already covers boy and son.
